notes.title: 34 years later, space sim Krellan Commander is back with a 2.0 release that's sort of FTL meets Dwarf Fortress
notes.notes:
At the time of Star Fleet II: Krellan Commander's release, I was still learning to spell and wrestling with the whole "going to the toilet independently" business, but if I'd had access to an MS-DOS PC between potty-training sessions, I dare say I'd have tried my hand at being an intergalactic warlord. Originally published in 1989 by Interstel Corporation and distributed by a little-known company called Electronic Arts, it's an absurdly in-depth and fiddly-looking space sim in which you fly around a randomly generated cosmos in your horrible Klingon-adjacent battlecruiser, blowing up or commandeering other ships, bombarding or invading planets, and generally speaking being a nuisance. 


According to its creators, Trevor Sorensen and Mark Baldwin, the game had a rushed launch that led to a lot of technical issues. The developers released another, relatively bug-free version in 1991, which is the version you'll find on most retro game preservation sites. Then, in 2018, Sorensen decided to make a new 2.0 version of Krellan Commander using his original 486 PC, which finally launched this week on Steam and GOG. 

 Read more

notes.title: A Quick Update
notes.notes:
Hey friends, 

Brian Rubin here! I've been getting some questions as to how the game is coming along so I wanted to chime in and give y'all a quick update! So far here's what's going on:

Delays:

Some real-life stuff has delayed us a bit, such as Trevor's floppy drive failing (he still programs the game on his 486) plus some deadlines he had for his other work at Interstel, such as satellite contracts! Those have pretty much passed, and the floppy drive is working again, so we're back on track.

What's Done:

The code audit is complete, which was a huge deal, and has made the game much more stable. 

What's Currently Being Worked On:

Right now much of the work is focusing on the documentation, as much of it has needed to be updated, but we're not far from being done on that. We've also made progress on the training manual as well. We're also working on a new trailer for the game

The State of the Game:

The current beta has been pretty rock solid. I've gotten some time with it and have had no bugs, and none of the other playtesters have reported any for a while, so the game feels as close as it's ever been to being complete.

Final Thoughts:

Only one person wants to get this game in your hands more than me, and that's Trevor himself. We're all working hard to get this game to you, but we want to do it right. I want to, again, thank you all for your patience and excitement for this game. 

Thanks for reading this quick update, and again for your patience. Y'all are the best.

Stay tuned, we'll have more soon!

notes.title: A Quick Update
notes.notes:
Friends, Brian Rubin here, and I just wanted to give you a quick update on how things are going with Star Fleet II 2.0! Work is still on going, but some things have admittedly slowed us down, such as:

[olist]
Trevor -- the lone developer -- not only had to finish up his semester of teaching along with other rocket scientist work, but he was also recently injured in his leg (nothing super major, thankfullly), which has slowed him down. He's recovering nicely, thank goodness, but it's obviously slowed things down a touch.
This one is my fault. We've been tweaking the last few missions of the game to make them, hopefully, better balanced. I've been banging my head against the penultimate mission for almost a year now, but I'm FINALLY close to finishing it. Sadly, something with my save game has been bugged, so Trevor has been working to fix it.  This has resulted in bugs fixed in the program itself as well, but of course it's taken time.
[/olist]
On the other hand, work on the game has been continuing. Many internal versions have been released, and we are THIS close to beta, when we lock down all new features and focused solely on bug hunting and fixing, as well as a code audit.

Oh, we also finally got accepted onto GOG! Yay! We'll be happy no matter where you buy the game, so wishlist it wherever you like, please and thank you. ;)

We've also begun work on some other things like a new trailer and updated documentation as well! 

So,  work HAS been happening, it's just we've all been too busy (me especially) to post about it, so I apologize for that. Please be sure we want to get the game to you as SOON as possible, we just want to do it right. The last thing we want, as I've said before, is a repeat of the problematic (and I'm being kind) 1.0 launch from 1989. 

I, therefore, want to thank you for your continued patience and excitement for this game. My excitement for this game hasn't waned even though I've probably put in around 1,000 hours into it at this point, and I cannot WAIT to get it to you.

Thanks again for your patience, and please don't hesitate to ask any questions if you have them. See you soon with more info!

notes.title: Starfleet II Development Update - 3/5/22
notes.notes:
My friends, Brian Rubin here, again coming to you with an apology for the lateness of this. Life has just been hectic as well, and getting Covid back in January DEFINITELY slowed me down, but now things have gotten to a point wherein I can put this dang dev update together for you all!

A lot has happened since our last update. The final big feature of 2.0 -- the captain's log, which integrates all the log files into a chronological, readable story about your mission -- is in, and currently being worked on, and we feel now we're just a few months away from releasing this thing into your grubby paws. On a personal note I just passed 100 episodes streamed of Star Fleet II, which has equaled roughly 250 hours of campaign play. This game is huge y'all.

Alright, without further adieu, here are the latest updates -- which include new features -- up to today, 3/5/22. Please note, pure bug fix releases were not included:


 11/19/21 - Version 1.9 Release 0.9 - Updates to how invasions are handled and displayed.
11/29/21 - Version 1.9 Release 1.01 - New indicator for planetary government types (unified/not unified) and lots of bug fixes. 
12/6/21 - Version 1.9 Release 1.03 - Updated line of sight priority for targets in orbit that are in LOS, along with bug fixes.
12/16/21 - Version 1.9 Release 1.04 - Expanded XO role, updated engine schematic, freighter power indicators and more, along with bug fixes.
1/9/22 - Version 1.9 Release 1.11 - The first iteration of the new Ship Information System, or SIS, has been implemented. This is an in-game reference library in which you can search for any number of topics, from torpedoes to boarding and everything in-between. We've been fleshing this out as we go and it is turning into something awesome. Eventually, it'll be a full in-game manual and wiki of sorts, we hope. This plus plenty of bug fixes.
2/18/22 - Version 1.9 Release 1.22 - The big one here is invasions. Whereas before, remote (AI-led) invasions would take several days, but now that take far less time to be more in-line with human-led invasions. This will be a massive boon in later, Admiral-level missions. 
2/19/22 -Version 1.9 Release 1.23 - More invasion-specific updates for this one. Now your XO will inform you when a remote invasion (AI-led) has begun, the strategic invasion display now shows cities captured or destroyed, and if more than half are invaded or destroyed, the planet may now surrender. 
2/20/22 -Version 1.9 Release 1.24 - The big one here is some probe-related QOL features, such as showing how many probes you have in the launch tubes and how many you have in storage, which is VERY helpful let me tell you.
2/22/22 - Version 1.9 Release 1.25 - Some QOL features regarding both landing parties and remote destroyers when they discover enemies in a system.

We've also had a lot of bug fix releases as well, which brings us up to v1.9 release 1.27 as of today. The next release should be 1.9 release 2.0, which might add some new stuff and should be coming within days. 

We now hope to have the game ready to release to you in a couple of months. Some things we still need to do, besides working on the game itself, is:


 Revise and update the documentation.
 Further update the Steam page with more new features.
 Come up with a new trailer for the game.

I feel like we're truly in the home stretch y'all. Thank you so much for your patience with us. We definitely want to bring you the most feature-complete and bug-free version of the game that we can. I'll try to do the next update in a more timely manner, and maybe that'll be the last one before release! Yay!

Thanks for reading, my friends, and please let us know if you have any questions. Be safe and well!

notes.title: Star Fleet II Development Update - 11/17/21
notes.notes:
My friends, welcome to the latest Star Fleet II Development Update. First off, let me apologize at the long amount of time between the last one and this one. Life kept getting busier and busier and I just never set aside the time to pound this out. I'm going to try to do this in little bits in the future so it won't be some massive thing in my mind, and therefore easy to avoid. If I chip away at it bit by bit, it'll be easier for me to get these to you.

Anyway enough about that, you're here to learn about what's been going on with Star Fleet II! The big word is: Probes. In recent updates, Trevor has added an entirely new way to use probes for Subadmirals and Admirals. Whereas before this new update, probes would go to a system, passively tell you what might be there in terms of planets, enemies, and starbases, and that was pretty much it.

Now, probes have an active mode that not only lets them go into orbit and scan planets, but also searches systems for enemy Starbases. It makes the exploration part of a mission MUCH more streamlined. That isn't to say it makes the game EASIER. Far from it. The probes help you find stuff more quickly, but you still need to deal with said stuff once you find it. Finding a UGA colony only a day or two into a mission does not make it any less of a challenge to deal with. 

There have been a TON of other updates and fixes as well, and you'll be able to read all about them in the release notes linked below (I'm sorry I don't have approximate dates for these). These are all for version 1.9. 


 Release 0.6 - Nav will check to see if there's a black hole in your path upon choosing a new navigational target. Full Notes Here.
 Release 0.7 - New Probes Systems for Subadmirals and Admirals. Full Notes Here.
 Release 0.71-0.73 - Exploring probes will optimize their routes more effectively to save energy. Full Notes Here.
 Release 0.80 - Changed the color of colonies in the planets table for easier identification. Full Notes Here.
 Release 0.81 - Starforts will now be more spread apart. Full Notes Here.
 Release 0.82/0.83 - Supply ships will now give updates on their ETA if requested again. Full Notes Here.
 Release 0.84 - Probes are now color-coded in the Probe Operations Control depending on their energy level. Full Notes Here.
 Release 0.86 - You'll now be asked if you wish to have a Destroyer explore a system if it thinks there are enemies there. Full Notes Here.

Now that the new Probe Operations Control is up and running, the next big feature Trevor plans to implement before 2.0 is the Captain's Log, which will be a personal journal of the captain. This will then be rolled into an all-encompassing Mission Log. This fully-integrated Mission Log will combine the Report Log, Message Log AND Captain's Log into one chronological document that details what happened during a mission. This is the final thing Trevor really wants to implement into the game before 2.0 finally launches, but it also might happen after 2.0 hits. We're not entirely sure yet. 

Regardless, this means we still don't have a final release date for the game, but it's looking less likely to be 2021. I'd reckon, at the rate things are happening, Q1, 2022 is far more likely. Please understand that we need to take the time to get this as stable, bug-free and well-documented as possible before releases, and we're all working hard, Trevor and playtesters like, to make that happen. We truly appreciate and thank you for your patience.

With that said, I hope you've enjoyed this development update, and I hope to catch you here on Steam, or YouTube or Twitch, every Monday morning for more Star Fleet II. Thanks for reading, and don't hesitate to hit us up if you have any questions. 

P.S. Don't forget, we're still actively looking for playtesters, as the more folks helping us find bugs, the quicker this will get released. Be sure to contact us if you have the time and interest, and thank you.

notes.title: July/August, 2021 Star Fleet II Development Update
notes.notes:
Hey friends, Brian Rubin here, and happy September! Sorry for the delay in this, I had a VERY busy July and August, to the point wherein only now are things slowing down and I have time to update y'all on the latest stuff going on with Star Fleet II!

First off, I wanna talk about release dates. Recently we pushed it back to October, but I'm gonna be honest, with the work that still remains, I'm not sure we'll be ready for October. This is not only due to the work that remains, but the fact that Trevor also basically has two other jobs: College Professor and Rocket Scientist, and September is going to be busy with both. So from now on, no release dates. We're gonna stick with "When it's ready" and hopefully get it out well before the end of the year, but again, we also want to do this right. We want to get the game to where Trevor wants it, feature-wise, and then work to get it as bug-free as possible for launch, as well as updating the necessary documentation. So while I'd LOVE for us to get it out in October, please understand if it's a smidge later than that.

Now, with that all said, let's get to the actual updates! We're now internally testing 1.9, which already has a ton of new features, such as armed freighters, a conditional firing mode that'll try to destroy warships and disable freighters and starliners, and some new toys in the Krellan arsenal. Here are the highlights, along with a download of the text file with all the updates for each version and release number. Please note, these should be opened in Wordpad. Now let's dive in, shall we?

Update Hightlights and Version Text File Downloads

Version 1.8


version 1.8 release 0.6 - A minor one, Circuit was changed to Patrol in the helm commands, plus several bug fixes. Download Text File.
v1.8 r1.1 - This one gives you an option to do an emergency stop if hit by a mine, or to keep going, plus other bug fixes. Download Text File.
v.1.8 r1.3 - This one adds a feature to set personnel transfer to the standard amount of crew for a prize crew of a captured ship automatically, plus numerous bug fixes. Download Text File.
v1.8 r1.4 - The big change here is that the default status for newly-captured enemies is now "Question" rather than "Hold", which can be a good and bad thing. ;) This plus numerous bug fixes. Download Text File.
v1.8 r1.5 - This one was entirely done to fix some bugs. Download Text File.
v1.8 r1.6 - Another purely bug-fixing release. Download Text File.
v1.8 r2.0 - This one adds numerous features, such as the invade command to Fleet Command, along with a new command called disperse, which will force all current local forces to disperse around your ship to about ten sectors. This is great for quick resupplies right before attacking a starbase or orbital forts, and also is great for spreading out your fleet just before such an attack so fewer are hit by mines. Planetary invasions also got some love, as now you can easily see how many surface-to-air lasers and planetary-defense-phasers a zone has, so you can focus on taking them out if need be. Your XO will now also ask you if you want to set your weapons to disable when attacking a freighter or starliner. Download Text File.
v1.8 r2.1 & 2.2 - This one adds a new visual indicator so you can quickly see if your escorts are resupplied in a starfort and all ready to go. Supply ships will now also restock crew and marines as well as supplies. Also, color coding has now been added to the data box so you can see at a glance if anything is in dire need of attention. Download Text File.
v1.8 r2.3 - A purely big fix release. Download Text File.
v1.8 r2.4 - This one adds more information as to where suspected starbases might be lurking to the intelligence screen, along with some bug fixes. Download Text File.


Version 1.9


version 1.9 release 0.1 - Version 1.9 adds a host of new features, such as new Krellan toys like the Klink Drive (a reverse-engineered version of the Blink Drive artifact, which lets you jump anywhere on the map) and the Nova Bomb (which was in a testing phase in this release), which can cause a system's sun to go nova. UGA freighters and Krellan troopships now have a single phaser for defense, and planetary defense for UGA colonies has been improved, sadly. ;) This is a big one y'all. Download Text File.
v1.9 r0.2 - Nova Bomb is ready for action, along with some bug fixes. Download Text File.
v1.9 r0.3 - For planetary invasions, you can now at a glance see the number of SALs and PDPs in a zone, plus some bug fixes. Download Text File.
v1.9 r0.4 - Conditional weapon setting added, which will now default to destroy for warships and disable for freighters and starliners when set in the weapons menu. Krellan-owned planets will now supply both you and your escorts, like a supply ship, plus some big bug fixes. Download Text File.
1.9 r0.5 - Missions 7-D and 7-D get clearer language for dealing with planets, plus several big bug fixes. Download Text File.


That does it for this round of updates! The game is coming along swimmingly and I could NOT be more excited about how it plays now. Every update makes me feel more and more like a proper starship captain/commander, and it's GREAT. I so can't wait to get this into your hands, folks. Thanks for reading, and don't hesitate to hit us up with any questions. Thank you!

notes.title: May (and Kinda June), 2021 Development Update
notes.notes:
Friends, first off let me apologize for the lateness of this. Work and life have just been super busy, in a good way really, and I've just not had the time to put this together, so this one is gonna be a bit truncated to save me time, but I'll be linking full version release notes so you can see for yourself how much has improved.

Here's the rundown:

In early May, 1,7 was released and it brought with it a whole bevy of new features. This includes:


A full career statistics screen that tallies everything from your first mission onward.
New quick navigation options, such as the nearest starbase, or a specific star system or planet from their respective information tables. 
New database options for looking at landing parties and bases.
New status screens for landing parties and Operation Big Brother.
New features to Fleet Command, such as see every ship's distance from you at a glance, or all their objectives.
New escort formations and a formation editor.
Orbital Fortresses, which are basically starbases orbiting UGA colonies.
Qships, warships disguised as freighters

1.7 received several patches, the notes to which you can read here:


1.7 Release 1.0 Notes (PDF)
1.7 Release 2.0 Notes (PDF)
1.7 Release 3.0 Notes (TXT)
1.7 Release 3.1 Notes (PDF)
1.7 Release 4.0 Notes (PDF)

In late May, 1.8 was released to select playtesters and brings with it even more new features, such as:


System search, which will now send your fleet in a sweep around a system. Handy for keeping your fleet together and looking for starbases or UGA ships.
Fleet command has received several new commands, such as multi-mode and local mode. Multi-mode allows you to select multiple ships and give them the same order easily. There are also keyboard shortcuts to select all warships, or all ships, or all battlecruisers, and so on. 
Fleet Command local mode only highlights ships in your system for selection, making it easy to only focus on the ships in your immediate vicinity. You can also see where everyone's position is using the new position command. 
As a Subadmiral or Admiral, you can order a moratorium on invasions from Fleet HQ, so that only you can order invasions. This is VERY handy in missions where you goals are planetary invasions. 
A new helm patrol mode, which will do an orbit around a specific object or point in space. Perfect for protecting Starforts. 
Slaves can now be converted to Krells, the game's currency, upon reaching the rank of Prefect. 
Improvements to planetary invasions. 

You can see the patch notes here:


1.8 Release 0.1 Release Notes (TXT)
1.8 Release 0.2 Release Notes (TXT)
1.8 Release 0.3 Release Notes (TXT) 
1.8 Release 0.4 Release Notes (TXT)

So as you can see, a LOT has happened and we're still trucking along toward what will hopefully be an August release. Thanks so much for your patience and for wishlisting the game, it is much appreciated. Until next time!

notes.title: April, 2021 Star Fleet II Development Update
notes.notes:
Hey friends, welcome to another Star Fleet II development update! This is gonna be a short one because there were two small updates this month:


1.6 Release 14 (4/5/21) - Mostly bug fixes like Krellan ships not moving as ordered and more.
1.6 Release 15 (4/7/21) - More bug fixes and stability fixes. This was the release that took us through the remainder of the month because it was pretty dang stable.

The rest of the month was dedicated to the next major version of the game, 1.7. I've not played 1.7 yet, in fact the only player to do so is the only playtester so far to win the game and become Imperial Tribune. Apparently we have a LOT to look forward to in 1.7, which might drop tomorrow as I write this. 

We're now hoping to hit 2.0 for release in August at this point. That could change of course, but right now that's what we're aiming for. 

Thanks for reading folks, and again, if you'd like to help us playtest this, please feel free to contact us. See y'all next month, and of course on the Monday morning streams!

notes.title: March, 2021 Star Fleet II Development Update
notes.notes:
Hey y'all, Brian here, and welcome to the March Star Fleet II development update. This was a pretty busy month, development-wise. Early in the month we got 1.6 Release 10, with new features to the CCC, improved mines, improved AI and much more, and release 10 got a bunch of patches to lead up to release 11, which dropped yesterday. Here are the details!


1,6 Release 10 (3/6/21) - This release included improvements to both enemy and friendly AI, new features to the CCC like a navigation command, improved/more deadly mines along with more ways to avoid them, such as slowing down and coming to a stop. Release 10 received around half a dozen patches throughout the month to fix various problems that cropped up, such as speeding through a minefield if your target was another system, or planetary invasion zone selection problems. 
1.6 Release 11 (3/30/21) - Much of the work leading up to Release 11 involved moving various functions to overlays so they take up less memory, and fixing more problems that cropped up as a result of issues with Release 10. As of this writing, it seems as if Release 11 is stable enough that Trevor can move forward working on the next major version of the game.


I seriously hope that, in the next entry, I'll be able to tell you about 1.7. It apparently has some new features that will make admiral's lives much more challenging. Trevor says it's mere weeks away, and he's teasing us a LOT with new features that he won't specify. 

Finally, we moved our internal playtest version from being standalone now to Steam! This will definitely help make sure we're all using the exact same version as we test for bugs and come up with ideas for new features. 

I couldn't be more excited about how development is coming along, and I can't wait to bring you this game once it's ready! Thanks for reading y'all, and I'll see you both next month for another dev update and in the Monday Star Fleet II streams! Have a great one y'all!

notes.title: February, 2021 Star Fleet II Development Update
notes.notes:
Hey friends, 

Brian here! I hope you all had a lovely, joyous and safe February! Now, you might recall at the end of the last entry, we talked about the tentative release of 1.6 release 8. Each "release" is an iteration that builds upon and fixes issues with the previous release, while each numbered version (i.e 1.6, 1.7, etc) denotes major new features and such, just to clarify. 

Well, just as we were testing 1.6 release 8, we ran into some snags with it, and so much work was done with it that it eventually evolved into release 9.


Release 9 (2/18/21) - This pretty big release includes fixes for mines, upgrades to the UGA AI (which is REALLY evident in higher-level missions), new commands (ALT-Y to go to the space forces table, for example), more information given about enemy starbases during an attack, improvements to escorts, improvements to the space forces table and a TON of other bug fixes.
Release 10 (in pre-release) - The problem with a game with as many moving parts as Star Fleet II is when you fix some bugs, you seem to generate others. Our playtesters have been finding more, and Trevor has been squashing them, so the next release should have even more bug fixes and a few new features, which will be detailed once it's fully-released in the next dev update. 


If you want to get an inkling as to how the sausage is made, you can read the full release notes PDF here.

If you want to see a bunch of these changes and improvements in action (especially the more aggressive enemy AI, whoooboy), check out my latest stream.

[previewyoutube=Srq_jZUUpM4;full][/previewyoutube]

It's hoped that we'll hit 1.7 in March, which as you know brings us that much closer to 2.0. If you have time and interest and want to help us bring the game to Steam that much sooner, please join our playtesting team! The more playtesters we have, the better! :)

That'll do it for this month's development update. Thanks so much to everyone who has wishlisted and followed us! We can't wait to bring 2.0 to you as soon as we all feel it's ready! :)

notes.title: January, 2021 Star Fleet II Development Update
notes.notes:
Hey friends, Brian Rubin/Space Game Junkie here, and welcome to our first monthly development update! This is something I figured we should do to keep y'all in the loop as to how development is progressing toward 2.0, so I'll whip this up on the last Friday of every month. I just thought of this a few days ago, so this entry will be a bit sketchy, but future entries should be...better. ;) With that said let's dive in. Keep in mind this is all for the current 1.6 branch:


Release 4 (1/3/21) - This corrected starliner routes, fixed tables for space foces, properly denoted which planet you've entered orbit of, fixed exiting fleet command and added some bombardment features for escorts. It also added more fluid escort movement to make them seem more realistic as they move through space.
Release 5 (1/11/21) - This added the hold fire all command, which is a very useful way for commanders at higher ranks (prefect and above) to stop firing on an enemy in case you need to get the kill shot or disable it. This also fixed memory problems.
Release 6 (1/17/21) - This added laptop-friendly keys, added more functionality to the hold fire all command in the space forces table, and big news, added more layers to capturing an enemy starbase. Now a starbase needs its shields, torpedoes and phasers all knocked out before it's marked as disabled and ready for boarding. 
Release 7 (1/24/21) - This fixed the never-ending space marines problem when trying to board a starbase. This also fixed memory problems, improved the notepad, and my favorite, added an indicator to the star systems table to denote which systems have enemy activity detected by your fleet.
Release 8 (Tentatively 1/30/21) - We're testing this one right now (I got over an hour with it today), and it fixes some bugs we discovered with release 7, like some planets not being able to be scanned or not being able to set default speed. In my hour I spent making bases and killing UGA ships, I only had one issue which should hopefully be fixed soon (engine sounds cutting out). 


So as you can see development is proceeding fairly rapidly. The hope is that release 8 of 1.6 is stable enough that Trevor can then move on and focus on adding new features for 1.7, which should hopefully drop in February. We'll keep you posted. Thanks for reading, and hail Zagar!

notes.title: Next Major Version Coming to Playtesters, Screenshots Released
notes.notes:
Friends, the notes for the next major version of the game, 1.6, have just been released to playtesters, and it's a DOOZY. Some of the major new features include:

New Combat Control Center

This new feature gives us a one-stop-shop for important controls while in the midst of combat, and it looks AMAZING.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39115985/2d09e7db5f96c198d1f7e7016539ff60f21bafe5.png 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39115985/1e50234e604a30c499a0d2b35dd4d04fdc9d2504.png

New Fleet Controls

When you reach the rank of Subadmiral, you have control over all friendly forces in the sector, and right now, to be honest, it's a bit clunky. This new fleet control system looks to really streamline controlling other ships, putting them into fleets and moving them where you need them. This will make coordinated attacks on things like enemy starbases so much more streamlined. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39115985/7dbd839231d176a6e5d203e71fdff866f5d01286.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39115985/3e711f57dbadde8f04a144919e778286d1b3122f.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39115985/ce06a1a938cdbf248e3dda921ddce1b1e6aae37e.png

And Much More

We're also getting a ton of other new features such as:


Upgraded escorts (they have phasers now!)
Integrated notepad
Quick navigation to specific planets, or planets with landing parties
Use of in-game currency to repair or upgrade your personal battlecruiser
Artifacts and experimental equipment


And this is all just for version 1.6, which us playtesters hope to get by the end of the month, if not sooner. Future versions should have even more goodies to the leadup to 2.0!

If you'd like to be a playtester and help us get the game to Steam even sooner, plus play with all these new toys, be sure to contact Trevor Sorensen using our site's contact form!

https://starfleet2.com/contact/

We can't wait to not only get our hands on 1.6, but to eventually bring 2.0 to Steam with all these goodies, bug fixes and more! Thanks for reading y'all!
